raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

`BlockTable.commit_block_table()` in the V1 model runner re-uploads the whole
active `[num_reqs, max_num_blocks_per_req]` block table host→device on every
step, for every KV-cache group, even when no row changed since the last upload.

A row only changes when a request is admitted, moved, removed, or crosses a
KV-block boundary. This PR tracks a conservative interval of rows changed since
the last commit that covered them and skips the copy when that interval lies
outside `[0, num_reqs)`. When it does copy, it is the same single contiguous
bulk transfer as today.

Model Runner V2 already avoids this (`StagedWriteTensor`), and #47936 (same
idea, per-row scatter) was closed for that reason. The V1 runner is still the
**default** on ROCm for `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM`, `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` and
`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` (`ROCM_DEFAULT_MRV1_ARCHITECTURES`, added in #53155 after
#47936 was closed), and on every platform when V2 is declined (ngram /
draft-model / suffix / medusa spec decode, elastic EP, DBO, SP at TP>1,
`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, ...). If V1 is going away soon enough that this
is not worth carrying, say so and I will close it.

**This is a CPU-overhead cleanup, not a throughput PR.** The whole
`commit_block_table` is ~58 µs of a 10–44 ms DeepSeek-V4-Flash step, so the
end-to-end ceiling is a fraction of a percent, and the e2e runs below are flat
within noise. What it removes is per-step host work and a host→device copy on
the compute stream whose size scales with
`num_reqs × max_model_len / block_size` per KV-cache group.

### Details

- `append_row` / `clear_row` / `move_row` / `swap_row` widen the dirty interval
  (`add_row` goes through `append_row`). `move_row` marks **both** rows: since
  #49757 it also zeroes the vacated source, and a later padded dummy-run commit
  must upload that zeroed row.
- `commit_block_table(num_reqs)` only transfers `[0, num_reqs)`, so rows dirtied
  at or beyond `num_reqs` stay dirty (`[num_reqs, hi]`) until a commit wide
  enough to cover them.
- The table starts fully dirty, so the first commit (a warmup dummy run) still
  performs the transfer. Without this every warmup commit is skipped and the
  first real request pays the first H2D copy from the pinned buffer — measured
  at 20–30 ms on GLM-5.3.
- Bookkeeping is two Python ints rather than a per-row numpy flag array: a flag
  array made the always-dirty case 12–16 % slower than main (numpy
  `.any()`/`.fill()` per group per step); the interval form is flat there.
- `mark_dirty()` for the two callers that write the host buffer directly and
  would otherwise lose their transfer: `model_executor/warmup/replayssm_warmup.py`
  and `distributed/elastic_ep/elastic_execute.py`.

## Test Plan

- 6 new unit tests in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py`, each checked
  against a plausible-but-wrong build: no initial dirty state fails
  `first_commit_copies_even_without_row_writes`; resetting the interval on
  every commit fails `keeps_rows_beyond_num_reqs_dirty` and
  `uploads_vacated_move_row_source`; marking only the `move_row` target fails
  `uploads_vacated_move_row_source`.
- Randomized differential test (outside the repo): 4000 steps × 3 groups × 2
  seeds of random add/append/clear/move/swap, direct host writes +
  `mark_dirty()`, full clears and random `num_reqs`; GPU[:n] == CPU[:n] after
  every commit.
- In-engine check: sync and compare the GPU and CPU block tables after every
  commit during a real generate run.
- Micro benchmark of `MultiGroupBlockTable.commit_block_table` using per-group
  dirty rates measured in the engine.
- GSM8K A/B with a base-repeat control, and `vllm bench serve` e2e, on
  DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (TP=1) and GLM-5.3 FP8 (TP=4), plus Llama-3.1-8B
  (takes V2, never reaches this code) as a no-op control.

## Test Result

8× MI355X (gfx950). main = `e6dc16cebd`, this PR rebased on it; vLLM nightly
`0.3.1.dev311+ge97573215` binaries with main's Python (no op-schema changes
between the two), torch `2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`. `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. Every
DeepSeek-V4 / GLM-5.3 run logged "Defaulting to V1 model runner".

**Correctness.** Differential test 0/24000 mismatches (the wrong builds above
give 76–898). In-engine: 0 mismatches over 7905 group-commits on
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, 7905 on DeepSeek-V4-Pro (13 layers, dummy weights), 1580
on GLM-5.3 (8 layers, dummy weights); the skip count equals the number of
commits whose content was unchanged, i.e. no over-copying.

**GSM8K** (5-shot, greedy, 1319 items, `max_model_len=4096`,
`max_gen_toks=256`, prefix caching off, seed 1234; `base2` = second run of the
unpatched build):

| model | base | PR | Δ | base2 − base | identical text: base/PR vs base/base2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | 0.9522 | 0.9507 | −0.0015 | −0.0076 | 33.1 % vs 32.8 % |
| GLM-5.3 | 0.9234 | 0.9249 | +0.0015 | −0.0091 | 27.0 % vs 27.4 % |
| Llama-3.1-8B (control, V2) | 0.7081 | 0.7058 | −0.0023 | −0.0023 | 96.4 % vs 98.0 % |

(strict-match.) No measurable accuracy change on GSM8K, within the base-repeat
noise floor.

**Where the skip applies** (in-engine, 150 prompts, ISL 1030, OSL 517,
`max_model_len=33000`):

| model | KV groups (block size, width) | concurrency | commits skipped | `commit_block_table` µs, main → PR (median / mean) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | 5: (64,516) (64,516) (256,129) (4,8256) (8,4128) | 50 | 66 % of group-commits, 0 % of steps | 58.3 / 62.3 → 37.1 / 36.4 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | same | 3 | 92 % of group-commits, 75 % of steps | 56.2 / 58.5 → 4.2 / 12.1 |
| GLM-5.3 (8 layers, dummy) | 1: (16,2064) | 50 | 74 % | 22.1 / 22.7 → 0.55 / 6.47 |

On DeepSeek-V4 the widest group (block size 4) changes on every step at 50
concurrent requests, which is why the gain there is partial.

**Micro** (`MultiGroupBlockTable`, CPU time per step including the row
mutations; each arm 4 consecutive runs, first discarded, median of 3, spread in
brackets):

| case | main µs | PR µs | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4 shape, 50 req, measured dirty rates | 28.49 [2.5 %] | 13.31 [2.2 %] | −53 % |
| DeepSeek-V4 shape, 3 req, measured dirty rates | 32.38 [8.5 %] | 0.92 [3.3 %] | −97 % |
| GLM-5.3 shape, 50 req, measured dirty rate | 6.35 [5.2 %] | 0.82 [2.4 %] | −87 % |
| 5 groups, every group dirty every step (worst case) | 30.65 [4.5 %] | 30.06 [1.5 %] | −2 % |
| 1 group, dirty every step (worst case) | 7.35 [1.2 %] | 7.30 [2.9 %] | −1 % |

**e2e** (`vllm bench serve`, random ISL 1030 / OSL 517, `--ignore-eos`, prefix
caching off, a fresh server per run; per server one 50-concurrency run of 253
prompts then one 3-concurrency run of 27 prompts; each arm 4 consecutive runs,
first discarded, median of 3, within-arm spread of total tok/s in brackets):

| model | conc | total tok/s main → PR | mean / median TPOT | mean / median TTFT |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, TP=1 | 50 | 5484.8 [1.12 %] → 5503.0 [0.39 %], +0.33 % | −0.36 % / −0.13 % | −0.60 % / 0.00 % |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, TP=1 | 3 | 862.4 [0.17 %] → 865.6 [0.26 %], +0.38 % | −0.32 % / −0.16 % | −1.16 % / −0.51 % |
| GLM-5.3 FP8, TP=4 | 50 | 2951.7 [0.68 %] → 2952.4 [1.10 %], +0.03 % | +0.10 % / −0.07 % | −0.93 % / +0.46 % |
| GLM-5.3 FP8, TP=4 | 3 | 470.5 [0.19 %] → 469.7 [0.08 %], −0.17 % | +0.21 % / +0.08 % | −0.75 % / −0.63 % |

All e2e deltas are within the within-arm spread; run-2→run-4 drift ≤ 0.9 % in
every block.

---

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Closing. On today's `main` the default model runner is V2 on every platform (#56360 removed the ROCm V1 defaults this PR relied on), and V2 never calls the V1 `BlockTable` copy. With V1 forced, an in-process counter on a varied-length workload skipped 0 of 200 copies, because one dirty row still uploads the whole table. #63373 removes Model Runner V1 and strips `block_table.py` along with it.

The rebased branch (onto `main@7128f568ac`, with dirty-marking for `GPUModelRunner.preserve_serving_state()` and the ReplaySSM warmup, plus writer-coverage tests) stays on `ZhengGong-amd:v1-skip-clean-block-table-copy` in case V1 removal stalls.

         num_tokens_padded=3,
     )
     assert dummy[0].tolist() == [PAD_SLOT_ID] * 3
+
+
+def _make_v1_block_table(max_num_reqs=4, max_num_blocks_per_req=8):
+    from vllm.v1.worker.block_table import BlockTable
+
+    return BlockTable(
+        block_size=16,
+        max_num_reqs=max_num_reqs,
+        max_num_blocks_per_req=max_num_blocks_per_req,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=64,
+        pin_memory=False,
+        device=torch.device("cuda"),
+        kernel_block_size=16,
+        cp_kv_cache_interleave_size=1,
+    )
+
+
+def test_v1_commit_block_table_skips_clean_copy():
+    """A commit that follows no row mutation must not re-issue the H2D copy:
+    at steady-state decode no row changes and the GPU table is already
+    current."""
+    block_table = _make_v1_block_table()
+    block_table.add_row([1, 2], row_idx=0)
+    block_table.commit_block_table(1)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert block_table.block_table.gpu[0, :2].tolist() == [1, 2]
+
+    copies = []
+    block_table.block_table.copy_to_gpu = lambda n=None: copies.append(n)
+    block_table.commit_block_table(1)
+    assert copies == []
+
+
+def test_v1_first_commit_copies_even_without_row_writes():
+    """Warmup dummy runs commit before any request writes a row; that first
+    commit must still copy, so the first real request does not pay for the
+    first H2D transfer."""
+    block_table = _make_v1_block_table()
+    copies = []
+    block_table.block_table.copy_to_gpu = lambda n=None: copies.append(n)
+    block_table.commit_block_table(2)
+    assert copies == [2]
+
+
+def test_v1_commit_block_table_keeps_rows_beyond_num_reqs_dirty():
+    """commit_block_table(num_reqs) only transfers the first num_reqs rows,
+    so a row dirtied past that prefix must stay dirty until a commit wide
+    enough to cover it, rather than being dropped."""
+    block_table = _make_v1_block_table()
+    # Dirty a row inside the prefix too, so the narrow commit really copies.
+    block_table.add_row([5], row_idx=0)
+    block_table.add_row([7, 8], row_idx=3)
+
+    block_table.commit_block_table(2)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert block_table.block_table.gpu[0, 0].item() == 5
+    assert (block_table.block_table.gpu[3] == 0).all()
+
+    block_table.commit_block_table(4)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert block_table.block_table.gpu[3, :2].tolist() == [7, 8]
+
+
+def test_v1_commit_block_table_uploads_vacated_move_row_source():
+    """Condensing moves the last row into a hole and shrinks num_reqs past the
+    vacated source. move_row zeroes that source on the host, and a later wider
+    commit (e.g. a padded dummy run) must upload the zeroed row rather than
+    leave stale block IDs on the device."""
+    block_table = _make_v1_block_table()
+    for row in range(4):
+        block_table.add_row([10 * row + 1, 10 * row + 2], row_idx=row)
+    block_table.commit_block_table(4)
+
+    block_table.clear_row(1)
+    block_table.move_row(3, 1)
+    block_table.commit_block_table(3)
+    block_table.commit_block_table(4)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert block_table.block_table.gpu[1, :2].tolist() == [31, 32]
+    assert (block_table.block_table.gpu[3] == 0).all()
+
+
+def test_v1_mark_dirty_forces_copy_after_external_write():
+    """Callers that write the host buffer directly must be able to force the
+    next commit to copy."""
+    block_table = _make_v1_block_table()
+    block_table.add_row([1], row_idx=0)
+    block_table.commit_block_table(1)
+
+    block_table.block_table.np[0, 0] = 42
+    block_table.mark_dirty()
+    block_table.commit_block_table(1)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert block_table.block_table.gpu[0, 0].item() == 42

issue_comments.body:
This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @ZhengGong-amd.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Closing. On today's `main` the default model runner is V2 on every platform (#56360 removed the ROCm V1 defaults this PR relied on), and V2 never calls the V1 `BlockTable` copy. With V1 forced, an in-process counter on a varied-length workload skipped 0 of 200 copies, because one dirty row still uploads the whole table. #63373 removes Model Runner V1 and strips `block_table.py` along with it.

The rebased branch (onto `main@7128f568ac`, with dirty-marking for `GPUModelRunner.preserve_serving_state()` and the ReplaySSM warmup, plus writer-coverage tests) stays on `ZhengGong-amd:v1-skip-clean-block-table-copy` in case V1 removal stalls.
